receipts.detail: Instrumenting the owner seam on the production sync path (5 nodes via buildNodeReadinessSyncCurrent) and the async authoritative-refresh path shows the seam source is EXACTLY {dimensions, runtimeAuthority, priorityControlPlaneRecovery, runtimeServeEligible, nodeEvidence, membershipPublication} on every call; every field is CONTENT-classified (membershipPublication digested with a per-frozen-object digest cache, its top-level createdAt/updatedAt observation-time); the key carries no table version and no planning segment (the publication table version only stamps the sync diagnostics memo); measured nesting 1/2/5/1/1/5 against the digest cap 16 (= the normalizer's own-data depth cap; live priority-recovery witness records measured by the verifier at depth 6-7). Map with source-owner justifications: solve/evidence/projection-readiness-per-node-generation-granularity-v2.dep-scope.md.

buildProjectionReadinessGeneration returns INCOMPLETE {unclassified_source_field | digest_depth_overflow | digest_domain_violation} for an extra seam field, a record nested past the cap, or any value the strict own-data normalizer would reject. The digest cap is the normalizer's PROJECTION_READINESS_MAX_OWN_DATA_DEPTH (16, imported) minus one because a seam field's value sits at normalizer depth 1 (verifier F5; receipt: field-relative depth 14 COMPLETE, 15 INCOMPLETE). Verifier F1 sealed: a null-prototype container at the cap and a hostile toString/Symbol.toPrimitive container fail CLOSED without any coercion (never a TypeError out of the evaluation). Verifier F2 sealed: a Date leaf, class instance, symbol key, accessor, non-enumerable key, sparse array, subclassed array, function leaf and Proxy are each INCOMPLETE (digest_domain_violation) while the plain twin stays COMPLETE; length-prefixed strings/keys keep the serialization injective (separator-forging strings, keys and flattened nestings digest differently). Integration: a field injected at the seam on the five-node cluster makes all 5 builds unowned (owned=0), and a cache WITHOUT any version surface memoizes soundly (1 build / 1 reuse / same reference) — v1 had to fail closed there and measured 704/864 unowned joiner builds in production. Verifier F4 sealed: a rejected value under an EXCLUDED observation-time key (Date under observedAt, function under enteredAt, Proxy under heartbeatAgeMs, accessor under observedAtMs, Date under the membership top-level createdAt, an over-deep container under observedAt) is INCOMPLETE, never aliased to its plain twin, while a plain observation-time value is still omitted from the key text. Verifier F6 sealed: a 5,000,000-length sparse array is rejected at the first hole (< 50 ms) and a non-enumerable array index stays COMPLETE (a data slot, as copyDenseOwnDataArray copies).

Five-node real-cache cluster (real SystemTableCache + real MembershipPublicationCoordinator sync read over a real membership publication row), production sync-read path, planning latch live: writes concerning node-1 only (heartbeat row + service row; the SERVICES version pushes every read past the CL-012 stored-snapshot layer to the owner seam) => node-1 rebuilds once, attributed to its node-scoped stamp (nodeEvidence); nodes 0/2/3/4: builds stay 1, each served by reuse, generation key byte-identical, and the returned projectionReadinessContract is the SAME reference (===).

After the node-1 write its new core carries the new evidence (raw.nodeEvidence.lastHeartbeat == new row value) and is a new reference; a semantic flip (node-1 status -> stopped) rebuilds node-1 with processAlive=false in both the snapshot dimensions and the owned core — no stale node-local entry — while the other four nodes keep their original core reference with builds==1.

A membership publication content change (epoch 2 row) rotates every node's generation (attribution 'membershipPublication'), rebuilds all five, and every new core's raw.membershipPublication.publicationEpoch == 2. Legitimate cluster-wide invalidation is not optimized away.

Two CONTROL_PLANE_PUBLICATIONS writes that bump the table version but leave the membership diagnostics' semantic content unchanged — an updated_at-only refresh of the winner row (the shape of ack/refresh writes) and an INSERT of a non-membership publication kind — rebuild NO node: builds stay [1,1,1,1,1], every core is the same reference, and the cores still carry the epoch-1 membership publication (11 seam reuses across both writes). This is the class that was 50% of v1's residual builds in production.

Stopping the control-plane service rows of node-1 and node-3 (serveEligible flips) rebuilds exactly node-1 and node-3 (new cores) while node-0/2/4 keep builds==1 and the same core reference — the affected set is exactly the nodes whose verdicts changed.

v2 DEP findings A/B/C/E preserved on the five-node cluster: (A) router state CONNECTED->READY for node-2 changes NO readiness dimension yet rotates node-2 only (raw nodeEvidence digested — stronger than v4), then DISCONNECTED rotates node-2 again on the node-scoped stamp; (B) a non-running lifecycle state for node-3 rotates node-3 only; (E) a repair record (identity recordedAt) for node-4 rotates node-4 only; (C) a publication-mode flip to repair_only rotates all five by content. In each step every other node reuses.

On the REAL SystemTableCache (versions bump synchronously, listeners fire on setImmediate): a sync read issued between a publication apply (epoch 2) and its deferred listener bypasses the diagnostics memo (stamped with the synchronous table version), rebuilds the seed with attribution 'membershipPublication' and its core carries epoch 2; after the listener the same fresh core is reused. Async: an evaluateNodeReadiness whose observation window straddles an epoch-3 apply is keyed by the epoch-2 content it actually observed; the next evaluation observes epoch 3, rebuilds (new reference, never the straddled core) and is then reused by reference. Finding recorded (separate owner, out of scope): the CL-012 stored-snapshot reuse layer has the same deferred-listener window.

A SERVICES write rotates the planning derivation version key (probed with an advancing numeric clock so the latch refreshes) and invalidates every stored snapshot, yet changes no verdict: all five nodes keep builds==1 and the same core reference. A planning change that flips a digested verdict (priorityControlPlaneRecovery.active for node-2) rotates exactly node-2, attributed to priorityControlPlaneRecovery. The planning snapshot reaches the core only through digested verdicts, so the segment was redundant (43% of v1's residual builds in production).

12 rounds of formation-shaped churn concerning node-1 (heartbeat + service row per round), planning latch LIVE, moving fixture clock, all five nodes read after each round through the production sync path: 17 builds / 56 reuses over 65 reads (86% reuse); each unaffected node exactly its initial build, reused on every round, zero node-local rotations, same core reference in every round; node-1 1+12 builds. Red-on-revert captured 2026-09-03 (scratch probes re-adding a key segment): restoring the six cluster-wide table versions => 65 builds / 8 reuses (12%), 148 assertions fail; restoring the planning derivation segment => 65 builds / 7 reuses (11%), 138 assertions fail — 'exactly the initial build across 12 rounds' and 'reused on every round' fail for every unaffected node in both, i.e. red through the intended mechanism.

Production wall clock, planning latch live: 10 rounds (20 cluster writes concerning node-1) with all five nodes read per round: each unaffected node exactly 1 build (its inputs never changed; zero builds attributed to its own segments or the membership publication); node-1 <= 1 + 10; total 15 builds <= 5 + 10 and < 20 writes x 5 nodes (the retired invariant). Under the six-version revert the same run needs 55 builds.

receipts.detail: Local docker 5-node formation (the A-characterization fixture), seed node, watchdog periodic samples, like-for-like first ~5.5 minutes: sync reads 85,163 -> 69,960 (caller count unchanged, ~13-14k/min); owner builds 47,402 -> 7,627 (-84%); reuse 8.6% -> 81.4% (formation windows 85-86%); builds per sync read 0.56 -> 0.11; owner build CPU 8,168 ms -> 1,844 ms; zero fail-closed builds; residual builds attributed 75% to each node's own heartbeat/transport evidence, 19% to verdict content, 1.9% to membership publication content, 0% to cluster-wide segments. Joiners reuse 65-81% (before 21-49%). Formation and schema admission completed; the run later failed in the known downstream ratings-partition family. Sealed bar (>= 50% reuse, <= 0.35 builds/read) met. Evidence: solve/evidence/projection-readiness-per-node-generation-granularity-v2.effectiveness-measurement.md. CPU caveat: the live run predates the round-2 normalizer-domain mirror in the digest; the verifier measured that mirror at ~43 us per evaluation (vs ~23 us in the measured build) on production-shaped seam records, about +0.8 s CPU per 5.5-minute seed window landing in the caller's sync-read section — the reuse and builds-per-read bar and the owner build CPU are unaffected because rotation semantics on production shapes are identical.
